entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-pw5q-rjx4-7f7p: Arcane: Delegated users:update permission allows admin account takeover via password reset (no privilege-hierarchy check)
entry.content:
Arcane: Delegated users:update permission allows admin account takeover via password reset (no privilege-hierarchy check)

Aliases: CVE-2026-96627

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

Affected:

  • github.com/getarcaneapp/arcane/backend/v2 — fixed in 2.6.0

## Summary A user holding the delegated `users:update` permission can reset the global administrator's password and take over the admin account. `UpdateUser` sets the target user's `PasswordHash` from the request body for ANY target with no comparison of caller-vs-target privilege. Because role assignment and role CRUD are deliberately gated by `RequireGlobalAdmin`, `users:update` is intended to sit BELOW admin (profile management); this finding defeats that separation. ## Root Cause `UpdateUser` (handler `backend/api/handlers/users.go:317-323`) loads the target by ID and sets `userModel.PasswordHash` from the request body for any user, then `userService.UpdateUser` (`user_service.go:174`) simply `tx.Save`s — with NO actor-vs-target privilege comparison. The only `IsGlobalAdmin` guard (`u…

entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-mp22-58ff-6fhr: Arcane: Environment access token bypasses the admin-required authorization gate on `/api/debug/pprof`
entry.content:
Arcane: Environment access token bypasses the admin-required authorization gate on `/api/debug/pprof`

Aliases: CVE-2026-96628

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N

Affected:

  • github.com/getarcaneapp/arcane/backend/v2 — fixed in 2.11.0

## Summary Arcane v2.10.2 contains an authorization inconsistency in `AuthMiddleware.managerAuth`. When a request supplies a valid environment access token through the `X-Arcane-Agent-Token` header, `managerAuth` resolves the associated environment, installs an environment-scoped permission set, and immediately calls `next(c)`. This occurs before the middleware evaluates the `AdminRequired` option and verifies that the caller is a global administrator. As a result, an environment-scoped access token can access routes protected with `WithAdminRequired()`, despite the corresponding `EnvironmentPermissionSet` intentionally containing no global or sudo permissions. In v2.10.2, the affected admin-only surface is the manager's Go `pprof` diagnostic interface under: `/api/debug/pprof/*` Th…

entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-74w3-63xv-x9mv: CoreDNS `k8s_external` headless AXFR can emit an empty transfer batch that panics the `transfer` plugin

CoreDNS `k8s_external` headless AXFR can emit an empty transfer batch that panics the `transfer` plugin

Aliases: CVE-2026-62994

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:L

Affected:

### Summary A network DNS client allowed to request AXFR for a CoreDNS zone can trigger a panic when CoreDNS is configured with `k8s_external` headless-service zone transfers and Kubernetes contains a headless service endpoint with no declared ports. entry.title: [NEW] GHSA-cv23-7vc5-jfh7: gomarkdown/markdown IsSafeURL panics on short URLs
entry.content:
gomarkdown/markdown IsSafeURL panics on short URLs

Aliases: CVE-2026-102941

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H

Affected:

  • github.com/gomarkdown/markdown — fixed in 0.0.0-20260724235538-61af6e1e6971

## Summary IsSafeURL slices url[:nPath] before checking that len(url) >= nPath, so a URL shorter than a path prefix (0, 1 or 2 bytes) triggers a slice-bounds panic, and this is reached end to end when the html.Safelink hardening flag is enabled and the input contains an empty or very short link destination, giving an unrecoverable crash DoS. Confirmed at HEAD (e08cff8; present since 2022). ## The defect parser/parser.go, IsSafeURL: ```go func IsSafeURL(url []byte) bool { nLink := len(url) for _, path := range validPaths { // "/", "./", "../" nPath := len(path) linkPrefix := url[:nPath] // line 789: sliced BEFORE the length guard if nLink >= nPath && bytes.Equal(linkPrefix, path) { // line 790: guard is too late ... ``…

entry.title: [UPDATED] GO-2026-5026: Invoking failure to reject ASCII-only Punycode-encoded labels in golang.org/x/net/idna
entry.content:
Invoking failure to reject ASCII-only Punycode-encoded labels in golang.org/x/net/idna

Aliases: CVE-2026-39821

Affected:

  • stdlib — fixed in 1.25.13, 1.26.6, 1.27.0-rc.3
  • golang.org/x/net — fixed in 0.55.0

The ToASCII and ToUnicode functions incorrectly accept Punycode-encoded labels that decode to an ASCII-only label. For example, ToUnicode("xn--example-.com") incorrectly returns the name "example.com" rather than an error. This behavior can lead to privilege escalation in programs using the idna package. For example, a program which performs privilege checks on the ASCII hostname may reject "example.com" but permit "xn--example-.com". If that program subsequently converts the ASCII hostname to Unicode, it will inadvertently permits access to the Unicode name "example.com".

entry.title: [UPDATED] GO-2026-6610: HTTP/2 transport accepts malformed framing-related headers in net/http
entry.content:
HTTP/2 transport accepts malformed framing-related headers in net/http

Aliases: BIT-golang-2026-78660, CVE-2026-78660

Affected:

  • stdlib — fixed in 1.26.9
  • stdlib — fixed in 1.27.2
  • golang.org/x/net — fixed in 0.60.0

Historically, we have been rather lax about malformed framing-related headers in our HTTP/2 implementation, as they cannot interfere with HTTP/2 framing. However, this makes it possible for our HTTP/2 implementation to forward responses containing such headers to an HTTP/1 client when acting as a reverse proxy. If the HTTP/1 client also does not behave strictly enough, this can result in response smuggling.

entry.title: [UPDATED] GO-2026-6605: HTTP/1 client connection desynchronization after CONNECT rejection in net/http
entry.content:
HTTP/1 client connection desynchronization after CONNECT rejection in net/http

Aliases: BIT-golang-2026-56866, CVE-2026-56866

Affected:

  • stdlib — fixed in 1.26.9, 1.27.2

When http.Transport sends an HTTP/1 CONNECT request with a non-empty Request.Body, it writes the body directly to the connection without framing after the request headers. If the server rejects the CONNECT request with a non-2xx keep-alive response, Transport returns the connection to the idle pool. Because CONNECT requests do not have a request body, the server may interpret the trailing body bytes as a subsequent pipelined HTTP/1.1 request on the connection, leaving the pooled connection desynchronized and causing the next caller that reuses it to read the response to the injected request. In reverse proxies (including httputil.ReverseProxy) that forward CONNECT requests through a shared Transport, this can lead to cross-user response poisoning.

References:

  • https://go.dev/cl/847306
  • https://go.dev/issue/81740
  • https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/U2fTuyDJznI

entry.title: [UPDATED] GO-2026-6617: HTTP/2 server crash due to HPACK encoder race in net/http
entry.content:
HTTP/2 server crash due to HPACK encoder race in net/http

Aliases: BIT-golang-2026-97032, CVE-2026-97032

Affected:

  • stdlib — fixed in 1.26.9
  • stdlib — fixed in 1.27.2
  • golang.org/x/net — fixed in 0.60.0

HTTP/2 servers could end up crashing due to inadvertently modifying its HPACK encoder concurrently. This happens because the server modifies the HPACK encoder from two goroutines without synchronization: one uses the encoder to encode a HEADERS frame as part of a response sent to a client and the other modifies the encoder's table size when handling a SETTINGS frame containing SETTINGS_HEADER_TABLE_SIZE that a client sends. A malicious client can repeatedly send a request while changing the header table size to crash the server.

entry.title: [UPDATED] GO-2026-6612: Double flow control refund on HTTP/2 server streams in net/http
entry.content:
Double flow control refund on HTTP/2 server streams in net/http

Aliases: BIT-golang-2026-78663, CVE-2026-78663

Affected:

  • stdlib — fixed in 1.26.9
  • stdlib — fixed in 1.27.2
  • golang.org/x/net — fixed in 0.60.0

The HTTP/2 server can refund connection-level flow control twice for the same data: Once when a client resets a stream (refunding data for any sent-but-unread portion of the stream), and again when a request handler reads the buffered data. A malicious client can exploit this to bypass the configured connection-level flow control limit (MaxReceiveBufferPerConnection). Total buffered data is still limited by the concurrent stream limit and stream-level flow control.

entry.title: [UPDATED] GO-2026-6603: HTTP/2 server memory exhaustion due to Trailer headers in net/http
entry.content:
HTTP/2 server memory exhaustion due to Trailer headers in net/http

Aliases: BIT-golang-2026-78659, CVE-2026-78659

Affected:

  • stdlib — fixed in 1.26.9
  • stdlib — fixed in 1.27.2
  • golang.org/x/net — fixed in 0.60.0

When "Trailer" headers are sent by a client, the HTTP server internally uses the header values to populate the Request.Trailer map passed to the server handler. Because Request.Trailer is a map, each entry incurs memory overhead. For HTTP/2 servers, a malicious client can exploit this by sending a "Trailer" header that declares a large number of fields, causing the server to allocate a disproportionate amount of memory while bypassing Server.MaxHeaderValueCount and Server.MaxHeaderBytes limits. This exploit is not applicable for HTTP/1 servers, which do not support multiplexing a large number of requests over one TCP connection, and whose Server.MaxHeaderBytes are calculated differently.

entry.title: [UPDATED] GO-2026-6613: HTTP/1 server connection desynchronization after 2xx CONNECT response in net/http
entry.content:
HTTP/1 server connection desynchronization after 2xx CONNECT response in net/http

Aliases: BIT-golang-2026-94439, CVE-2026-94439

Affected:

  • stdlib — fixed in 1.26.9, 1.27.2

When an HTTP server handler sends a 2xx response to an HTTP/1 CONNECT request and returns without hijacking the connection, the server improperly continues to read and serve requests from the connection. Since a 2xx response to an HTTP/1 CONNECT converts the connection into a tunnel, the server should not treat the connection as continuing to contain HTTP. The impact of this misbehavior is mostly limited to potential request smuggling, where an intermediate proxy considers the data on the connection to be tunneled and the server considers it to be HTTP.

The repository must use SSH. `http`, `https`, and `socks5` proxy URLs all take this path…

Reject malformed ECH outer extension references in crypto/tls

Aliases: BIT-golang-2026-97031, CVE-2026-97031

Affected:

  • stdlib — fixed in 1.26.9, 1.27.2

Multiple ECH outer extension references are not permitted under RFC 9849; previously, a client could send a well-crafted packet that could trigger memory exhaustion in the server process by specifying multiple references. We now reject these as malformed and curb the memory amplification vector as a result.

References:

  • https://go.dev/cl/847312
  • https://go.dev/issue/81855
  • https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/U2fTuyDJznI

entry.title: [UPDATED] GO-2026-6600: Recognize yield as regexp preceder keyword in html/template
entry.content:
Recognize yield as regexp preceder keyword in html/template

Aliases: BIT-golang-2026-97030, CVE-2026-97030

Affected:

  • stdlib — fixed in 1.26.9, 1.27.2

A trusted template author may have previously written a valid template wherein the use of the 'yield' keyword would not be correctly escaped. We now ensure that valid keyword uses are escaped and non-keyword uses are not escaped.

References:

  • https://go.dev/cl/840925
  • https://go.dev/issue/81823
  • https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/U2fTuyDJznI
